subject: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@meridianco.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@meridianco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist, the next immediate milestone is a short acceptance sprint focused on concurrency behavior and tail-latency at two production-ish load points. The goal: validate the 99th percentile latency stays below 220ms at steady-state throughput of 350 qps, and verify throughput scaling to 700 qps with graceful degradation (error rate <= 0.3%).

I attached a lightweight acceptance matrix and a proposed load plan. High level timeline we propose:
- Week 1 (this week): baseline smoke + KV-cache warmup (dev staging)
- Week 2: concurrency sweep (350 qps steady-state; 700 qps peak ramps)
- Week 3: artifacts & sign-off (results export, raw traces)

Action items for MeridianCo:
1) Share a service account and test key for the sandbox cluster (or confirm we may reuse the ephemeral token we provisioned).
2) Confirm target dataset size for representative inference (you mentioned ~18 tokens aver. payload).
3) Point us to any IP allowlist or egress constraints.

Attachments: meridianco-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (matrix + pass/fail criteria), loadplan-concurrency-sweep.json (k6-style load plan).

I cc’d Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (inference eng) — they’ll own execution and result collection. I’ll coordinate demos and the final readout.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
[Attachment: meridianco-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)]
[Attachment: loadplan-concurrency-sweep.json (json)]

From: Elena Costa <elena.costa@meridianco.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@meridianco.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@meridianco.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo

Hi Laura —

Thanks — this looks sensible. A few clarifying questions before our infra team hands you the sandbox credentials:
1) What exact payload distribution should we be using? We have two common payload profiles (short = 12 tokens, medium = 26 tokens).
2) Will Redwood’s run include KV-cache priming or do you want us to send warmup traffic from our side?
3) For the 700 qps peak, do you expect token-level billing to spike significantly? Our finance team flagged potential cost impact.

We can supply the service account once you confirm the payload and warmup approach. Also, can you include the expected artifact formats for the readout (csv of raw latencies, aggregated percentiles, and the collection of pprof traces or flamegraphs)?

Best,
Elena Costa
Engineering Manager, MeridianCo
elena.costa@meridianco.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-31T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo

Quick internal note on execution approach:
- We will run the concurrency sweep from our dedicated staging pool (isolated tenant), so MeridianCo does not need to spin infra. We just need the sandbox key and allowed egress CIDR.
- Warmup: Redwood will perform an automated KV-cache priming pass (3k requests at ramped concurrency) prior to measured runs. This avoids cold-start noise.
- Payload: we should run the short and medium profiles Elena mentioned and report percentiles per profile. The acceptance matrix will mark the profile that defines the contract (prefer medium if you want production realism).
- Artifacts: we’ll produce: raw-results-YYYYMMDD.csv (per request), aggregated-percentiles.json, and a tarball with pprof snapshots. We’ll also produce a short notebook that computes SLO pass/fail and cost delta at the tested points.

I’m attaching a slightly modified loadplan that uses 30s steady windows (helps tail measurement) — will push final versions to the Drive link and include in the readout.

-Karthik
Sr. Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
[Attachment: loadplan-concurrency-sweep.json (json)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Costa <elena.costa@meridianco.com>, Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@meridianco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:52:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo — run results (raw + summary)

Hi team —

We completed the concurrency sweep today from staging (runs executed against the sandbox credentials Elena provided). Summary highlights:
- Medium profile (26 tokens): 350 qps steady-state -> 99p = 198ms (PASS vs 220ms target).
- Peak ramp to 700 qps: 99p = 342ms, error rate = 0.21% (degradation observed but within the 0.3% threshold).
- Short profile (12 tokens): 350 qps 99p = 132ms; peak 700 qps 99p = 228ms (PASS).

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: raw-results-20260902.csv, aggregated-percentiles.json, pprof-traces.tar.gz. Small notes: a hot-spot appeared at sustained 600+ qps tied to repeated long-tail KV lookup patterns for a particular prompt template — we isolated the queries and attached examples in the results csv.

Next suggested steps:
1) Run a follow-up targeted test on the KV lookup template (we can do this with you or hand the test case to your infra).
2) If MeridianCo is comfortable with the observed degradation characteristics, sign-off on the acceptance matrix and we’ll schedule production rollout windows.

Attachments: raw-results-20260902.csv

Thanks,
Ben Carter
SRE / Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: raw-results-20260902.csv (csv)]

From: Tom Reeves <tom.reeves@meridianco.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Costa <elena.costa@meridianco.com>, Procurement <procurement@meridianco.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Sprint: Concurrency sweep & tail-latency audit for MeridianCo — run results (raw + summary)

Laura / Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear artifact set. MeridianCo reviews the results and we’re OK to accept the matrix conditional on two items:
- Redwood runs the targeted KV-template test you called out and shares the delta with and without a small prompt rewrite (we want to understand practical mitigations).
- Our finance contact gets a short note with the estimated per-token cost delta for the 700 qps steady case (Ben / Karthik, can you provide a 1-paragraph cost delta for accounting?).

If those are provided by EOD next Tuesday (2026-09-08), Procurement will sign the acceptance matrix and we’ll schedule the production rollout.

Tom Reeves
VP Engineering, MeridianCo
tom.reeves@meridianco.com
